statements.text: Stretching the texture once across a large plane is tiling.
statements.explanation: Stretching is scaling, not repeating.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Without repeat mode, the edge pixels stretch instead of the image repeating.
statements.explanation: Clamp mode extends the edge pixels.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The tiling scale is the number of repeats across a surface.
statements.explanation: The scale decides how finely the texture repeats.

statements.label: D
statements.text: An engine repeat setting can make a non-seamless image seamless.
statements.explanation: Seamlessness is a property of the image content.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Distinctive features that recur at a regular spacing show as visible repetition even without a seam.
statements.explanation: Repeating features form a pattern the eye notices.

questions.stem: A game has music, sound effects, dialogue and interface clicks, with separate sliders for music and effects. Check each statement that is true about the audio design.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Headroom is the loudest level that distortion is allowed to reach.
statements.explanation: Headroom is the margin kept below the digital maximum so sums do not clip.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Each volume slider sets the volume of its own bus.
statements.explanation: Each slider acts on one bus.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Decibels are a linear, absolute scale.
statements.explanation: Decibels are logarithmic and relative.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Ducking automatically lowers the music bus while dialogue plays and restores it afterwards.
statements.explanation: Ducking keeps speech intelligible.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Separate buses for Music, SFX and Dialogue can each feed the Master bus.
statements.explanation: Buses give independent control and feed the output.

questions.stem: A modeller and a coding agent need to talk about the parts of a polygon mesh. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A quad is a face with four sides.
statements.explanation: Quad is the name for a four-sided face.

statements.label: B
statements.text: An n-gon is a face with more than four sides.
statements.explanation: N-gon is the term for a face with five or more sides.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Triangulation is the step that merges two separate meshes into one object.
statements.explanation: Triangulation splits faces into triangles; it does not merge meshes.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A vertex is a single point with a position in 3D space.
statements.explanation: A vertex is a point; edges and faces are built from vertices.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A face is a straight line that joins two vertices.
statements.explanation: A straight line joining two vertices is an edge; a face is the surface bounded by edges.

questions.stem: A modelling tool shows a face count and an engine profiler shows a triangle count for the same mesh. Check each statement that is true about the two measures.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A quad contributes two triangles to the triangle count.
statements.explanation: A quad is split along a diagonal into two triangles.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Face count and triangle count are two names for the same number.
statements.explanation: A quad is one face but two triangles, so the numbers differ.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Triangle count is the number of triangles left once the faces have been triangulated.
statements.explanation: GPUs draw triangles, so the triangle count is taken after triangulation.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Vertex count and triangle count measure the same thing.
statements.explanation: Vertices are points; triangles are surfaces made from three of them.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A five-sided face triangulates into five triangles.
statements.explanation: An n-sided face gives n minus 2 triangles, so five sides give three.

questions.source: Vertex count in the tool versus on the GPU
questions.stem: An interviewer says: 'My modelling tool reports 8 vertices for a hard-edged cube, yet the engine's profiler reports 24.' Check each statement that is true as an explanation.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A profiler that reports more vertices than the modelling tool has miscounted.
statements.explanation: The two tools count different things: corner positions versus full GPU vertices.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A UV seam forces the GPU to split a vertex because the two sides have different UV coordinates.
statements.explanation: The same position with two UV values is two GPU vertices.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A hard edge gives the corner a different normal on each face, so the GPU keeps a separate vertex per normal.
statements.explanation: A different normal at the same position needs a duplicated GPU vertex.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A GPU vertex carries attributes such as a normal and UV coordinates in addition to a position.
statements.explanation: A GPU vertex bundles position, normal and UV, so differing attributes mean a new vertex.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Smooth shading raises the vertex count by giving each face its own normal at a corner.
statements.explanation: Smooth shading shares one normal at a corner; separate normals per face describe flat shading.

questions.stem: An imported crate has a normal map assigned, yet a teammate asks the agent to 'fix the normals'. Check each statement that is true about the two terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A normal is a direction perpendicular to a surface, used for lighting.
statements.explanation: Normals are the geometry directions that lighting uses.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A normal map changes how light is worked out for each pixel and leaves the geometry unchanged.
statements.explanation: The detail is a lighting effect, not new geometry.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A normal map adds real triangles to the mesh to make the surface bumpy.
statements.explanation: A normal map is image data and leaves the triangle count alone.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A normal map is a texture that stores a direction per texel to fake fine surface detail.
statements.explanation: The map holds per-texel directions that bend the lighting.

statements.label: E
statements.text: 'Recalculate the normals' and 'replace the normal map' are the same instruction.
statements.explanation: One edits the mesh's face directions, the other edits or swaps an image.

questions.stem: Some faces of an imported crate look black or vanish when viewed from outside. A developer tells the agent 'fix the shading'. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Smooth shading and flipped normals are the same problem.
statements.explanation: Smooth shading is how normals are shared across faces; flipped normals are a wrong direction.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Backface culling means deleting the rear faces of an object from the file.
statements.explanation: Culling is a drawing-time skip and leaves the file unchanged.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Faces whose normals point into the object are described as having flipped normals.
statements.explanation: Flipped normals are inside-out faces.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Backface culling skips drawing a face when it is seen from the side its normal points away from.
statements.explanation: The renderer discards faces seen from behind, which is why inward faces vanish.

statements.label: E
statements.text: 'Fix the shading' is as precise as 'recalculate the normals so they point outward'.
statements.explanation: The first phrase does not name the cause; the second names both the term and the direction.

questions.stem: A coding agent builds a crate mesh and a wood texture. The texture is missing on one object and looks stretched on another. Check each statement that is true about the terms involved.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Unwrapping lays the 3D surface out flat in 2D to produce the UV map.
statements.explanation: Unwrapping produces the flat layout that the UV map stores.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A UV map gives each vertex a 2D coordinate in the texture.
statements.explanation: UVs link surface points to image points.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Stretched wood grain points to a poor UV layout rather than a low-resolution image.
statements.explanation: Stretching comes from layout versus surface shape, not the pixel count of the image.

statements.label: D
statements.text: U and V name the axes of texture space, which keeps them distinct from the X, Y and Z of 3D space.
statements.explanation: Texture space has its own axes, named U and V.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A texel is one corner of a mesh face.
statements.explanation: A texel is one pixel of a texture.

questions.stem: A post has a metal pole and a red cloth pennant, held in two material slots on one object. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A material slot is a position on an object that holds a material, and faces are assigned to a slot.
statements.explanation: Faces point at slots and slots hold materials.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A material and a texture are two words for the same image.
statements.explanation: A material is a shading description; a texture is one possible input to it.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A texture is an image; a material describes how a surface is shaded and may use textures as inputs.
statements.explanation: Textures feed materials; they are different things.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Extra materials on one object add triangles to the mesh.
statements.explanation: Materials change draw cost, not the number of triangles.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A draw call is the count of triangles in a mesh.
statements.explanation: A draw call is a request to the GPU to draw a batch; it is not a triangle count.

questions.stem: A door model rotated by script swings about its middle instead of its edge, and a 1 m crate sinks halfway into the floor placed at y = 0. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The origin, also called the pivot, is the point an object's position and rotation refer to.
statements.explanation: Origin and pivot are the reference point for transforms.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A 1 m crate with its origin at the centre sits exactly on the floor when placed at y = 0.
statements.explanation: A centred origin puts half the crate's height below y = 0.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Moving the origin in the modelling tool drags the visible mesh along with it.
statements.explanation: The origin can be moved while the geometry stays where it is.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The phrase 'make a door' already tells the agent where to put the pivot.
statements.explanation: The phrase names the object, not its pivot.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A swinging door needs its pivot on the hinge edge.
statements.explanation: Rotation happens about the origin, so it belongs at the hinge.

questions.stem: A modeller thinks in centimetres and builds a tree 540 units tall; the engine treats one unit as one metre. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Scale and size mean the same thing.
statements.explanation: Size is the extent of the mesh; scale is a multiplier carried by the object or node.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Scaling the tree node down repairs the mesh data itself.
statements.explanation: A node scale hides the problem on that node while the mesh stays the wrong size.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A model built in centimetres and imported as metres appears one hundred times too large.
statements.explanation: The numbers are kept but read in larger units.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Unit and scale are two names for one property.
statements.explanation: A unit is a measure of distance; scale is a multiplier.

statements.label: E
statements.text: In Godot a unit is conventionally read as one metre.
statements.explanation: The engine's convention is one unit equals one metre.

questions.stem: A cube mesh is 2 m across. The modeller scales the object to (0.1, 0.1, 0.9) to make a pole and exports without applying transforms. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Applying transforms is a step done in the engine after import.
statements.explanation: The step belongs in the modelling tool before export.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A non-unit scale on the imported node is inherited by anything built from it, such as a collider.
statements.explanation: A node scale propagates to its children.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Applying the scale changes how the pole looks in the viewport.
statements.explanation: Apply keeps the look and changes only where the numbers are stored.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Applying the scale bakes it into the vertex positions and resets the object's scale to 1.
statements.explanation: Apply moves the scale into the vertices.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Before applying, the mesh data can describe a different size from the size the object appears.
statements.explanation: The vertices still describe a 2 m cube; the object scale makes it look like a pole.

questions.stem: A modelling tool treats +Z as up, while glTF and Godot treat +Y as up. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Blender uses +Z as up, while glTF and Godot use +Y as up.
statements.explanation: That is why a conversion is needed between Blender and Godot.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Unreal's editor treats +Z as up, as Blender does.
statements.explanation: Unreal's editor is Z-up.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Up axis names which axis points up; handedness names whether the axes follow a right-hand or left-hand rule.
statements.explanation: They are two separate properties of a coordinate system.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A model that lies on its side after import suggests the up axis was not converted on export.
statements.explanation: The height stays on the old up axis, so the model appears tipped.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Up axis and handedness are two names for the same setting.
statements.explanation: Fixing one leaves the other unchanged.

questions.stem: A developer asks a coding agent to 'export the model for the engine'. Check each statement that is true about the formats named.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A .gltf file is the single binary form, and .glb is the text form.
statements.explanation: The roles are swapped: .gltf is text plus separate data files.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A .glb file packs a glTF asset into one binary file.
statements.explanation: GLB is the single-file form.

statements.label: C
statements.text: OBJ carries skeletal skinning and animation along with geometry.
statements.explanation: OBJ lacks skinning and animation.

statements.label: D
statements.text: glTF is an open interchange format for 3D assets.
statements.explanation: glTF is an open standard for moving 3D assets between tools.

statements.label: E
statements.text: One glTF asset can describe meshes, materials, textures, skins and animations together.
statements.explanation: glTF's scene description covers a whole rigged, textured prop.

questions.stem: A level has a stone archway the player walks through. A developer asks the agent for 'accurate collision'. Check each statement that is true about the shape terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A convex hull is the smallest convex shape that encloses the mesh, so on an archway it fills the opening.
statements.explanation: A hull cannot have a hole, so it blocks the doorway.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A concave (trimesh) shape follows the mesh triangles, so it can keep the archway opening passable.
statements.explanation: A trimesh follows the triangles exactly, holes included.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A convex shape has no dents or holes.
statements.explanation: Convex means any line between two inside points stays inside.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Primitive shapes, such as box, sphere and capsule, are made of the mesh's own triangles.
statements.explanation: Primitives are simple analytic shapes and not built from the mesh.

statements.label: E
statements.text: In Godot a concave shape works on moving bodies as well as static ones.
statements.explanation: Godot restricts concave shapes to static bodies.

questions.source: Collision shape is not the visual mesh
questions.stem: A character model has 30,000 triangles including a cape and a sword. A developer says to the agent: 'use the model's mesh as its collider'. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: 'Add a collider' already names the shape and size.
statements.explanation: The phrase leaves shape and size open.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A collider should copy the cape and the sword so they block the player as they look.
statements.explanation: Copying protrusions makes the character catch on scenery.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A collision shape is authored separately from the visual mesh and can be much simpler.
statements.explanation: Collision geometry is a separate design choice from the visible mesh.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A capsule is a common primitive shape for a character body.
statements.explanation: A capsule slides smoothly past edges and is cheap to test.

statements.label: E
statements.text: 'Use the mesh as the collider' asks for a concave (trimesh) shape, which is a poor fit for a moving character.
statements.explanation: A trimesh is the slowest option and works on static bodies only in Godot.

questions.source: Collision shape choice by body type
questions.stem: A stone archway is fixed in the level, a large rock is fixed in the level, and a crate is pushed by the player. The developer picks collision shapes in Godot. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A single convex hull on the archway keeps the opening passable.
statements.explanation: A convex hull fills the opening.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The pushable crate should use a trimesh shape in Godot.
statements.explanation: Godot allows concave shapes on static bodies only.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The archway is a static body.
statements.explanation: A fixed object that other bodies collide with is a static body.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A concave shape suits the archway because the opening stays passable.
statements.explanation: A concave shape can follow the hole.

statements.label: E
statements.text: The pushable crate is a moving body, and a box primitive suits it.
statements.explanation: A body moved by the simulation is a moving body, and a primitive is cheap.

questions.stem: A scene has 50 identical trees. A developer asks the agent to add levels of detail (LOD). Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A visible jump when the engine switches versions is called aliasing.
statements.explanation: The visible switch is called popping; aliasing is jagged edges.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Extra LOD meshes add no storage or load time.
statements.explanation: Each version is more data to store and load.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The engine picks the LOD version by distance or screen size.
statements.explanation: Smaller on screen means a cheaper version.

statements.label: D
statements.text: LOD reduces the number of trees that are drawn.
statements.explanation: LOD lowers the triangles per tree and leaves the tree count alone.

statements.label: E
statements.text: LOD keeps several versions of a mesh with decreasing triangle counts.
statements.explanation: That is the definition of level of detail.

questions.stem: A developer asks a coding agent to build a crate with a Python file that uses bpy and runs Blender in background mode. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A script that ends without an error has produced a verified asset.
statements.explanation: A clean run can still encode a wrong size, axis or scale.

statements.label: B
statements.text: bpy is the name of Blender's Python API.
statements.explanation: bpy gives scripts access to Blender's data and operators.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A script is a reproducible recipe that can be reviewed, diffed and rerun.
statements.explanation: A file is an artifact that can be versioned and rerun.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A script run in background mode is unable to read the mesh or export a file.
statements.explanation: The same data operations and exports run without a window.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Background mode runs Blender with no window.
statements.explanation: Background mode is also called headless: no interface is shown.

questions.stem: A developer connects a coding agent to Blender through an MCP server and an add-on. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The model itself runs inside the Blender process.
statements.explanation: The model stays in the agent; Blender only executes the calls.

statements.label: B
statements.text: MCP is a standard way for an agent to discover and call tools that another program exposes.
statements.explanation: It defines how tools are listed and called.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The add-on receives the tool calls and carries them out in Blender.
statements.explanation: The add-on is the Blender side of the connection.

statements.label: D
statements.text: MCP is a file format for storing meshes.
statements.explanation: MCP is a protocol for tools and has nothing to do with mesh storage.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A run-code tool without guards lets whoever can reach the connection run code as the user.
statements.explanation: Unchecked code execution is a real exposure, so keep it local and trusted.

questions.stem: A developer wants numbers a headless test can check after import: a post meant to be 0.2 x 1.8 x 0.2 m with Y up, standing on the floor at y = 0, at unit scale. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A bounding box lists the names of the materials on the mesh.
statements.explanation: Materials are read from the surfaces, not from the bounding box.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A bounding box of (0.2, 0.2, 1.8) in a Y-up engine suggests the post lies on its side.
statements.explanation: The 1.8 m height sits on Z instead of Y.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A lowest point at y = 0 relative to the origin shows the pivot is at the base.
statements.explanation: The base touching the origin height means the object stands on the floor.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A node scale of (1, 1, 1) suggests the transforms were applied.
statements.explanation: An unapplied scale would show as a non-unit value.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A bounding box is the smallest box that encloses the mesh, and its extents give width, height and depth.
statements.explanation: Extents are the box's size along each axis.

questions.stem: A developer compares phrases for a crate request to a coding agent. Check each statement that is true about which phrase names a term precisely.

statements.label: A
statements.text: 'Add a collision shape' names the shape and its size.
statements.explanation: It leaves the shape and size to the agent.

statements.label: B
statements.text: 'Origin at base centre' names the pivot.
statements.explanation: It states where the origin goes.

statements.label: C
statements.text: 'As a .glb' names the export format.
statements.explanation: GLB is a specific format.

statements.label: D
statements.text: 'Export it with the usual settings' names the up axis and scale.
statements.explanation: The phrase names no axis or scale; defaults vary.

statements.label: E
statements.text: 'Under 200 triangles' names a budget that can be checked.
statements.explanation: A triangle count is a number a test can read.

questions.stem: A developer moves between engines and wants the collision terms straight. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Godot's concave shape corresponds roughly to Unreal's complex collision.
statements.explanation: Both mean exact triangle collision.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Simple and complex collision are the same shape in Unreal.
statements.explanation: They are two different shapes used for different jobs.

statements.label: C
statements.text: In Unreal, simple collision is made of primitives and convex hulls.
statements.explanation: Simple collision uses cheap shapes.

statements.label: D
statements.text: In Unreal, complex collision is the per-triangle mesh.
statements.explanation: Complex collision tests the exact triangles.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A simulated Unreal object should use complex collision for its movement.
statements.explanation: Simulated bodies rely on simple shapes.

questions.source: Say it to the agent: prop request wording
questions.stem: A developer tells an agent: 'Make me a barrel in Blender and put it in my game so the player can bump into it.' Check each statement that is true about which term the vague phrase hides.

statements.label: A
statements.text: 'Bump into it' leaves open whether a solid collider or a trigger is meant.
statements.explanation: Collision can mean blocking or only reporting.

statements.label: B
statements.text: 'Not lying on its side' is a statement about the up axis.
statements.explanation: Orientation depends on which axis is up.

statements.label: C
statements.text: 'Standing on the floor' is a statement about the pivot or origin.
statements.explanation: Where the origin sits decides whether the barrel rests on y = 0.

statements.label: D
statements.text: 'The right size' is a statement about the pivot.
statements.explanation: Size is stated in metres, and the unit convention decides it.

statements.label: E
statements.text: 'Cheap to draw' is stated with a triangle budget and a material count.
statements.explanation: Triangle count and material count are the measurable budgets.

questions.stem: An imported model arrives with a problem. Check each statement that pairs the symptom with the term that most likely explains it.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A prop that sinks halfway into the floor points to the up axis.
statements.explanation: Sinking points to the origin sitting at the prop's centre.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A prop that lies on its side points to handedness.
statements.explanation: Lying on its side points to the up axis, not handedness.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A prop about one hundred times too large points to a unit mismatch.
statements.explanation: Centimetres read as metres give a factor of one hundred.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A prop with an odd non-unit node scale points to backface culling.
statements.explanation: An odd node scale points to a scale that was not applied.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A prop that rotates about the wrong point points to the material slots.
statements.explanation: Rotating about the wrong point points to the origin.

questions.stem: A coding agent can drive Blender through an MCP session or through a bpy script. Check each statement that is true when comparing them.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A script and an MCP session are the same artifact.
statements.explanation: One is a file, the other a conversation of calls.

statements.label: B
statements.text: MCP suits exploring an open scene or making a one-off fix.
statements.explanation: Live calls fit exploration and quick edits.

statements.label: C
statements.text: An MCP session leaves a transcript of tool calls.
statements.explanation: Each call and result appears in the conversation.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A bpy script is a file that can be rerun to regenerate the asset.
statements.explanation: A script is a recipe that gives the same asset when rerun.

statements.label: E
statements.text: For a prop that has to be regenerated later, an MCP session is a better record than a script.
statements.explanation: A single file is easier to diff and rerun than a transcript.

questions.stem: A team is cutting rendering cost for a scene of trees with two materials each. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A trimesh collision shape adds draw calls.
statements.explanation: Collision shapes are not drawn.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Triangle count and draw call count measure the same cost.
statements.explanation: Triangles are surface work; draw calls are batch requests.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Merging two materials that share a look reduces draw calls.
statements.explanation: Fewer materials usually mean fewer batches.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A draw call is the count of triangles in a mesh.
statements.explanation: A draw call is one request to draw a batch.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Merging materials changes the triangle count.
statements.explanation: Merging materials leaves the geometry alone.

questions.stem: Three symptoms appear on imported models. Check each statement that matches the symptom to the term that explains it and the phrase that fixes it.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Many draw calls on one object point to many material slots.
statements.explanation: Each material typically adds a draw call.

statements.label: B
statements.text: 'Reduce the object to two materials, merging slots that share a look' is a precise fix for the slot problem.
statements.explanation: It states a number and what to merge.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A missing or stretched texture points to absent or poorly laid-out UVs.
statements.explanation: UVs link the surface to the image.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A stretched texture points to inward normals.
statements.explanation: Normals affect lighting, not how an image is laid on the surface.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Black or invisible faces point to inward normals.
statements.explanation: Lighting and culling depend on the direction a face points.

questions.stem: An agent reports that an exported prop 'looks right'. Check each statement that is true about what a headless check and a person can each establish.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Whether a collider feels fair is for a person to judge.
statements.explanation: Feel is a human judgement.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A headless test can judge whether the prop looks good under the game's lighting.
statements.explanation: Appearance under lighting needs a person looking at a render.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Reading the lowest point against the origin catches a prop that sinks or floats.
statements.explanation: The lowest point relative to the pivot shows resting height.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A headless test can assert the bounding box, the node scale and the material names.
statements.explanation: These are numbers that can be read and compared.

statements.label: E
statements.text: 'Looks right' and 'measures right' mean the same thing.
statements.explanation: A model can look right on screen while a number is wrong.

questions.stem: A designer wants a coin that adds to the score when the player touches it while the player walks straight through. The developer asks a coding agent for 'a coin collider' in a 2D Godot game. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: 'Collider' is used for solid shapes and detection regions alike, so the word leaves the role open.
statements.explanation: The agent might build a solid body that stops the player.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A detection region works from the pixels of its sprite and needs no collision shape.
statements.explanation: Detection reads the collision shape; the sprite is only a drawing.

statements.label: C
statements.text: An Area2D reports overlaps and does not block the body that enters it.
statements.explanation: An area is a detection region that reports overlap and applies no response.

statements.label: D
statements.text: 'A trigger area on the coin that removes it when the player enters, without blocking' names the role, the event and the non-blocking requirement.
statements.explanation: Each element of the behaviour is named.

statements.label: E
statements.text: An Area2D pushes the player back slightly on contact.
statements.explanation: Pushing back is a solid body's response, not an area's.

questions.stem: Engines use the word 'collision' for two jobs: a solid collider and a trigger. Check each statement that is true about the two terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A trigger reports that something entered but not that something left.
statements.explanation: Triggers report leaving as well, for example body_exited in Godot.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Layers and masks do not affect which objects a trigger detects.
statements.explanation: Layers and masks still decide what a trigger can detect.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A solid collider produces a collision response such as blocking, while a trigger just reports an overlap.
statements.explanation: Response is the difference between the two.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Switching a solid collider to a trigger keeps it blocking the player and adds enter events.
statements.explanation: A trigger lets other colliders pass through it.

statements.label: E
statements.text: In Unity one collider can be solid and a trigger at the same time.
statements.explanation: A collider is either solid or a trigger, so blocking and sensing need two colliders.

questions.source: Collider versus trigger, say it to the agent
questions.stem: A developer writes: 'Add a wall on the right edge of the room that detects when the player touches it.' The agent adds an Area2D, and the player walks out through the wall. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The word 'wall' guarantees that the agent builds a blocking body.
statements.explanation: The agent built what was literally written, so the brief should say the player must be stopped.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A wall that blocks needs a solid body such as a StaticBody2D with a collision shape.
statements.explanation: A static body supplies the blocking and a child area can supply the touch event.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The word 'detects' asks for a detection region, while 'blocks' asks for a solid body.
statements.explanation: The instruction named only the detection role.

statements.label: D
statements.text: In Unity, enabling Is Trigger on the wall's collider makes the wall block more firmly.
statements.explanation: A trigger collider lets other bodies pass through.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Adding layers to the area's mask makes the area block the player.
statements.explanation: A mask chooses what is scanned and gives no blocking.

questions.stem: Godot's 2D physics has several node types, and the type decides who moves the body and who handles contact. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A CharacterBody2D is simulated like a RigidBody2D, so gravity needs no code.
statements.explanation: A character body has collision detection but no physics simulation.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A RigidBody2D is moved by the physics simulation, so it is driven with forces or impulses.
statements.explanation: A rigid body is a dynamic body owned by the simulation.

statements.label: C
statements.text: An Area2D detects overlapping bodies, can change gravity or damping inside it, and does not block.
statements.explanation: Detection and influence are the jobs of an area.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A StaticBody2D is a fixed obstacle that other bodies collide with.
statements.explanation: Static bodies suit walls and floors.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A CharacterBody2D detects collisions and leaves the response to code.
statements.explanation: The response comes from move_and_slide or move_and_collide.

questions.stem: Unity sorts colliders as static (a collider with no Rigidbody), dynamic (a Rigidbody with Is Kinematic off) and kinematic (a Rigidbody with Is Kinematic on). An elevator is moved by code each physics step. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A static collider is a collider that has a Rigidbody and is moved by code.
statements.explanation: A static collider has no Rigidbody.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A dynamic body is moved by the physics engine in response to gravity, forces and collisions.
statements.explanation: Dynamic bodies respond to the simulation.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A kinematic body is moved by code and not by forces, and it can push dynamic bodies in its path.
statements.explanation: Kinematic motion comes from outside the simulation, yet the body still acts on others.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The elevator should be dynamic, because dynamic bodies are the ones moved by code.
statements.explanation: Dynamic means the simulation owns the motion; code-driven motion is kinematic.

statements.label: E
statements.text: In Godot, a StaticBody2D plays the kinematic role for a platform moved by code or animation.
statements.explanation: The Godot node for a code or animation driven platform is an AnimatableBody2D.

questions.stem: An agent builds a 2D platformer player as a CharacterBody2D. In _physics_process it adds gravity to the velocity, sets horizontal velocity from input and calls move_and_slide(). Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A CharacterBody2D is simulated by the engine in the same way as a RigidBody2D.
statements.explanation: A character body is code-driven; a rigid body is simulated.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The movement belongs in _physics_process, which runs at the fixed physics rate, not in the per-frame callback.
statements.explanation: Collision movement runs in the fixed-rate physics callback.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Overwriting a RigidBody2D's position each frame is the recommended way to move it.
statements.explanation: Rigid bodies are driven with forces or impulses.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The gravity line is needed because a character body is not simulated; the code supplies it.
statements.explanation: Nothing pulls a character body down unless the code changes its velocity.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Velocity should be multiplied by delta again before move_and_slide() is called.
statements.explanation: move_and_slide() applies the time step itself.

questions.stem: In Godot every collision object has a collision layer and a collision mask. Check each statement that is true about the two terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Layer and mask are one setting seen from two sides.
statements.explanation: They are two independent fields.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Changing an object's layer also changes which layers it scans.
statements.explanation: Layer and mask change separately.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The mask is the set of layers an object scans for contacts.
statements.explanation: Mask says what an object looks for.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The layer is the set of layers an object appears in.
statements.explanation: Layer says where an object can be found.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Object A detects object B when B's layer is among the layers in A's mask.
statements.explanation: Detection runs from the scanner's mask to the other object's layer.

questions.stem: In the Godot editor collision layers are numbered, while in scripts collision_layer and collision_mask hold a bitmask integer. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A mask value of 0 scans the full range of layers.
statements.explanation: A mask of 0 scans no layers.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Values of several layers are multiplied together to form the mask.
statements.explanation: Values add, since each layer is a separate bit.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Writing a layer number where a bit value is expected can select the wrong layer.
statements.explanation: A number mistaken for a bit value points at a different layer.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A bitmask is an integer in which each layer has its own bit.
statements.explanation: A bitmask packs the layers into one integer.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Layer 3 has the value 3 in a script, the same number the editor shows.
statements.explanation: The script value for layer 3 is 4.

questions.source: Layers and masks, say it to the agent
questions.stem: Enemies should bounce off walls and the player but pass through one another. The developer tells the agent only: 'make the enemies not collide with each other'. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: In Unity, unticking the World/Enemy pair makes enemies pass through each other.
statements.explanation: That change would let enemies pass through walls.

statements.label: B
statements.text: In Unity the matching change is to untick the Enemy/Enemy pair in the layer collision matrix.
statements.explanation: That pair controls enemy-enemy contact.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Disabling the enemies' collision shapes meets the request.
statements.explanation: It also removes contact with walls and the player.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A precise instruction puts enemies on their own layer and sets their mask to scan the wall and player layers but not the enemy layer.
statements.explanation: Layers and masks pick which pairs interact.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Making enemies heavier meets the request, because mass decides whether contact is detected.
statements.explanation: Mass affects the response, not detection.

questions.stem: An icy floor should let the player slide, and a rubber ball should bounce. A designer tells an agent 'make the floor slippery and the ball bouncy'. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Slippery maps to low friction and bouncy maps to high bounce, both set on a physics material.
statements.explanation: A physics material holds surface properties such as friction and bounce.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Friction and bounce are separate properties of a contact.
statements.explanation: A slippery floor can have no bounce at all.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A round collider is what makes a ball rebound.
statements.explanation: Rebound comes from the bounce value of the contact, not from the outline.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Lowering a body's mass is how to raise its bounce.
statements.explanation: Mass sets how hard a body is to accelerate and is a separate property.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A glossy render material is what makes the player slide.
statements.explanation: A render material changes only how the surface is drawn.

questions.stem: A raycast asks the physics world what is the first thing hit by a ray from an origin in a direction for a given length. Check each statement that is true about the term.

statements.label: A
statements.text: By default Godot's ray query does not report Area nodes.
statements.explanation: Areas are reported only if the query asks for them.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A hitscan weapon, whose shot lands instantly, is usually built on a raycast.
statements.explanation: The shot is an instant line test along the aim direction.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A basic ray query reports the nearest hit along its path.
statements.explanation: The result describes a single first hit.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A ray has width, so it reports objects in a narrow cone around the line.
statements.explanation: A ray is an infinitely thin line.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A ray from an enemy's eyes to the player tests line of sight.
statements.explanation: If the first hit is the player, nothing solid is in between.

questions.stem: A bomb should damage the enemies within 3 metres in any direction. Check each statement that is true about a shape query (overlap query) and a raycast.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A shape query returns the objects that overlap a given shape, such as a sphere.
statements.explanation: A shape query tests a region at this moment.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A ray covers a line, not a region.
statements.explanation: A ray is a single line.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A shape query finds trigger regions and does not report solid bodies.
statements.explanation: Shape queries test colliders in general, solid bodies included.

statements.label: D
statements.text: One ray from the bomb finds the enemies in the whole area around it.
statements.explanation: A 3 metre region needs a shape query or many rays.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A ray is used to ask who is near, and a shape query to ask what stands between two points.
statements.explanation: The roles are swapped: a shape query finds who is near and a ray checks what is in between.

questions.stem: A small, fast bullet passes through a thin wall now and then, with continuous collision detection off. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Tunnelling happens because a fast body's layer stops being recognised by the wall's mask.
statements.explanation: Layers do not depend on speed.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Tunnelling is a fast body passing through a thin obstacle because overlap is tested at discrete positions instead of along the path.
statements.explanation: Nothing checks the space between two tested positions.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A thicker wall can reduce tunnelling, but a fast enough body can still skip it.
statements.explanation: Wall thickness helps, but skipping depends on the step distance.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Continuous collision detection costs more per body, so it suits fast, small bodies.
statements.explanation: The extra cost is why it is switched on selectively.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Continuous collision detection tests the path swept during a step.
statements.explanation: It tests the swept path, not only the end position.

questions.stem: A developer asks an agent for a crate knocked away by an explosion, a rocket that speeds up while its engine burns, and a paddle that moves at 300 px/s while a key is held. Check each statement that is true about force, impulse and velocity.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Setting a body's velocity and applying an impulse are the same operation.
statements.explanation: Setting velocity replaces the motion, while an impulse adds to it.

statements.label: B
statements.text: An impulse is an instantaneous change of momentum applied once.
statements.explanation: The explosion knock-back is a one-time impulse.

statements.label: C
statements.text: An impulse is a faster force that changes position directly.
statements.explanation: Both change velocity and not position directly.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A force acts over time and produces acceleration.
statements.explanation: Constant force means steady acceleration.

statements.label: E
statements.text: The rocket's engine is modelled as one impulse at launch.
statements.explanation: Sustained thrust needs a force applied over time.

questions.stem: A designer asks an agent to 'move the platform right at 100 pixels per second' and to 'teleport the player to the checkpoint'. The player is a CharacterBody2D. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A velocity of (100, 0) and a velocity of (-100, 0) are the same velocity.
statements.explanation: They have equal speed but opposite directions.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A CharacterBody2D has no velocity property.
statements.explanation: move_and_slide() reads and updates a velocity property on a character body.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Writing a body's position directly is a teleport that skips collision handling along the path.
statements.explanation: A teleport has no sweep and no response, so a destination in a wall can embed the player.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Writing position runs the same collision handling as move_and_slide().
statements.explanation: Only the move functions run collision handling.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Velocity has a speed and a direction; speed is its size.
statements.explanation: Velocity is a vector; speed is its magnitude.

questions.stem: Collision handling has two stages: detection and response. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A body's bounciness belongs to detection.
statements.explanation: Bounce shapes the response, the speed returned after contact.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A trigger applies a blocking response after it detects an overlap.
statements.explanation: A trigger detects and applies no response.

statements.label: C
statements.text: move_and_slide() stops at the first contact and returns the details, while move_and_collide() applies a sliding response.
statements.explanation: The functions are swapped: move_and_collide() stops and reports, move_and_slide() slides.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Detection finds that and where two shapes overlap, and response decides what then happens.
statements.explanation: The two stages are separate.

statements.label: E
statements.text: For a RigidBody2D the developer writes the code that stops it at a wall.
statements.explanation: The simulation supplies the response for rigid bodies.

questions.stem: A game renders at 30, 60 and 144 frames per second on three machines, and its physics runs on a fixed time step. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The per-frame callback runs at a variable rate.
statements.explanation: It runs once per rendered frame, and frame times vary.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A fixed time step advances the physics simulation in equal increments of game time.
statements.explanation: The step size is constant regardless of frame rate.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The engine may run zero, one or several physics steps for one rendered frame.
statements.explanation: Physics catches up or waits to keep its own clock steady.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Multiplying by delta in the per-frame callback makes collision results the same on the three machines.
statements.explanation: Delta fixes speed but not collision tests, jump arcs or contact timing.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A variable time step gives the same jump arc on the three machines.
statements.explanation: Different step sizes give different integration results.

questions.stem: A melee game team uses three terms: hitbox, hurtbox and body collider. Check each statement that is true about the melee convention.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A body collider is the solid shape that blocks movement.
statements.explanation: Blocking is the body collider's job.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The sword carries the hurtbox and the enemy carries the hitbox.
statements.explanation: The roles are swapped: the sword carries the hitbox.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Hitboxes and hurtboxes are normally solid colliders.
statements.explanation: Both are detection regions that report overlap and do not block.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A hitbox is a region that deals damage during an attack.
statements.explanation: The hitbox is the attacking region.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A hurtbox is a region on a character that receives damage.
statements.explanation: The hurtbox is the receiving region.

questions.stem: A developer briefs an agent on a sword swing that should damage a given enemy once. Check each statement that is true about the setup.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The hitbox should be active during the frames of the swing in which the blade can hurt.
statements.explanation: The active frames limit when damage can occur.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The sword's hitbox mask should scan the player's own layer so it detects the wielder.
statements.explanation: The mask should scan the enemies' hurtbox layer and not the player's own.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Once-per-swing damage is automatic because an overlap is a single event.
statements.explanation: Overlap lasts several steps, so the swing needs a record of targets already hit.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The hurtbox can sit on a layer separate from the body collider's layer.
statements.explanation: Separate layers let masks choose which shape is scanned.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A constantly active hitbox is fine, because overlap is just detection.
statements.explanation: An always-on hitbox would damage things outside the attack.

questions.stem: A platformer has ledges the player can jump up through from below, then stand on. In Godot 2D this is a collision shape with one-way collision enabled. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A one-way platform is a solid collider that blocks from one side, normally the top.
statements.explanation: It is solid from one direction and open from the other.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A one-way platform is a trigger that lifts the player onto it.
statements.explanation: Triggers neither block nor lift.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A ledge on a layer that the player's mask does not scan behaves the same as a one-way platform.
statements.explanation: The player would also pass through from above and not stand on it.

statements.label: D
statements.text: One-way collision works on a shape that belongs to an Area2D.
statements.explanation: One-way collision has no effect under an Area2D.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Dropping through can be done by briefly turning off collision with that ledge.
statements.explanation: A short pause lets the player fall past it.

questions.stem: Lava should hurt the player every 0.5 s while the player stands in it. The agent built an Area2D whose body_entered handler subtracts 1 health, and the player loses health only once. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: An event reports a change, while a query reports the current state.
statements.explanation: Which bodies overlap now is a query, not an event.

statements.label: B
statements.text: body_exited fires repeatedly while the player stays inside.
statements.explanation: An exit event fires once when the player leaves.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A timer that asks which bodies currently overlap the lava gives repeated damage.
statements.explanation: Polling the overlap list repeats the check while the overlap lasts.

statements.label: D
statements.text: body_entered is an enter event that fires once when an overlap begins.
statements.explanation: Standing still inside produces no further enter events.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Making the lava's shape bigger produces repeated enter events.
statements.explanation: Size does not change the fact that entry is a single event.

questions.stem: A player is invulnerable for 3 seconds. An enemy that was already overlapping the player when invulnerability ends does not hurt the player until it leaves and re-enters. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Making the detection shape larger fixes the missed damage.
statements.explanation: Shape size does not create a new event.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A fix is to query the current overlapping bodies when invulnerability ends.
statements.explanation: A query reads the current state.

statements.label: C
statements.text: An enter handler is a query of the current overlaps.
statements.explanation: A handler reacts to an event and does not read the current state.

statements.label: D
statements.text: No new enter event fires when invulnerability ends, so the earlier overlap stays unreported.
statements.explanation: An enter event is a change, and nothing changed.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Godot's body_entered signal also works as a stay event.
statements.explanation: body_entered fires once at the start of an overlap.

questions.stem: Three engines name the same idea differently: a region that reports objects inside it without blocking them. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: In Godot this is an Area2D or Area3D.
statements.explanation: An area is Godot's non-blocking detection region.

statements.label: B
statements.text: In the three engines the region detects through its drawn mesh or sprite.
statements.explanation: Detection uses collision shapes, not drawings.

statements.label: C
statements.text: In Unreal this is a collision component whose response to the other object's type is Overlap.
statements.explanation: Overlap is Unreal's non-blocking response.

statements.label: D
statements.text: In Godot an area detects a body when the body's layer is among the layers in the area's mask.
statements.explanation: Layer says where an object appears and mask says what is scanned.

statements.label: E
statements.text: In Unity this is a collider with Is Trigger enabled.
statements.explanation: Is Trigger turns a collider into a detection region.

questions.source: Ground check, say it to the agent
questions.stem: A developer tells an agent: 'only let the player jump when touching the ground'. The player is a CharacterBody2D. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Floor, wall and ceiling are different classes of contact surface.
statements.explanation: 'Touching' is ambiguous, so the brief should say the contact must be a floor.

statements.label: B
statements.text: is_on_floor() reflects the result of the most recent move_and_slide() call.
statements.explanation: It is updated by the movement call and is not live.

statements.label: C
statements.text: An Area2D at the feet detects solid ground when its mask scans the ground's layer.
statements.explanation: Areas report only bodies on layers in their mask.

statements.label: D
statements.text: is_on_floor() is a plain overlap test that is true when the body is inside a floor shape.
statements.explanation: It classifies contact by surface direction and is not an overlap test.

statements.label: E
statements.text: An empty ray result from the feet means the player stands on the ground.
statements.explanation: An empty result means the ray hit nothing within its length.

questions.stem: A developer swaps a character's sprite for a larger drawing, and afterwards the arms poke into walls. Check each statement that is true about the terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A debug view that draws collision shapes at runtime exposes the mismatch.
statements.explanation: Seeing the shape over the art shows where they disagree.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Replacing the sprite resizes the collision shape.
statements.explanation: The shape is a separate node and keeps its size.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Capsule shapes are costly to test and so are avoided for characters.
statements.explanation: Primitives such as capsules are cheap to test.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The physics engine reads collision shapes, not the picture.
statements.explanation: Collision comes from shapes.

statements.label: E
statements.text: The engine leaves the transparent pixels of a sprite out of the collision.
statements.explanation: Transparency is a rendering property and does not affect collision.

questions.source: Say it to the agent: collider versus trigger
questions.stem: A developer gives an agent: 'Add a collider to the shield pickup so that the player can collide with it and get the shield.' Check each statement that is true about wording the request with exact terms.

statements.label: A
statements.text: 'Walk through it and collect it' asks for a detection region.
statements.explanation: A pickup is an area or trigger.

statements.label: B
statements.text: 'It should not block movement' is a useful clause in the brief.
statements.explanation: The word 'collide' alone leaves blocking open.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A sprite alone is enough for a detection region to find the player.
statements.explanation: A detection region needs a collision shape.

statements.label: D
statements.text: 'Stop the player at it' asks for a solid body.
statements.explanation: Blocking is a solid body's response.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A good observable result is that the player passes through and the shield state is set once.
statements.explanation: The result can be checked in a test.

questions.stem: A teammate says 'collider, trigger and raycast are all just ways of finding out that two things touched'. Check each statement that is true in correction.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A raycast blocks things in its path.
statements.explanation: A ray does not block, push or notify.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Collider, trigger and raycast are three names for one detection tool.
statements.explanation: They differ in what they do and what they return.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Walls and floors are fitting uses of a solid collider.
statements.explanation: A collider produces a response such as blocking.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A pickup or damage zone is a fitting use of a raycast.
statements.explanation: A pickup or damage zone is a trigger; a ray suits line of sight or a hitscan shot.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A raycast is a query along a line, not a body in the world.
statements.explanation: A ray asks a question at one moment.

questions.stem: A 2D game has walls, a player, enemies, bullets and coins, and each kind of object must interact with only some of the others. Check each statement that is true about layers and masks in Godot.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Detection runs from the scanner's mask to the other object's layer.
statements.explanation: A scans B only if B's layer is in A's mask.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Giving each kind of object its own layer lets masks choose which pairs interact.
statements.explanation: Separate layers are the first step in the design.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A function that takes layer numbers avoids the bit-value mistakes of writing the integer directly.
statements.explanation: Layer numbers are converted to bits by the function.

statements.label: D
statements.text: With each object on the default layer and scanning it, each object collides with each other object.
statements.explanation: That is why the default is unsuitable for selective interaction.

statements.label: E
statements.text: The default layer already separates walls from enemies.
statements.explanation: The default puts them on one layer.

questions.source: Fixed time step, say it to the agent
questions.stem: A jump written in the per-frame callback reaches a different height on a 30 frames-per-second machine than on a 144 frames-per-second machine. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A constant step makes behaviour depend on the frame rate.
statements.explanation: A constant step makes behaviour reproducible and testable.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A long variable step lets a fast body travel farther than a thin wall is thick in one step.
statements.explanation: Long steps let fast bodies skip thin obstacles.

statements.label: C
statements.text: 'Make the movement frame-rate independent' names the callback.
statements.explanation: It states a goal without naming the callback.

statements.label: D
statements.text: 'Apply gravity and call move_and_slide() inside _physics_process using the physics delta' names the callback.
statements.explanation: It names the callback and the delta to use.

statements.label: E
statements.text: The per-frame callback is the right place for movement that collides.
statements.explanation: Collision movement belongs in the fixed-rate callback.

questions.stem: A bullet is a RigidBody2D that sometimes tunnels through a thin wall. Check each statement that is true about remedies and what each costs.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A hitscan design still needs a physical bullet body.
statements.explanation: Hitscan has no travelling bullet.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A higher physics rate is a remedy that costs more for the whole simulation.
statements.explanation: More physics steps per second shrink the distance between tested positions, at a cost to the whole simulation.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Continuous collision detection is a remedy that costs more per body.
statements.explanation: It tests the swept path of each body.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Tunnelling is guaranteed for a fast body.
statements.explanation: It depends on where the tested positions fall relative to the wall.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A raycast from the previous position to the new position is a remedy that needs more code.
statements.explanation: The ray checks the path between positions.

questions.source: Static, kinematic, dynamic and character bodies
questions.stem: A developer must brief an agent on a 2D platformer by choosing a body type for each object. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: An elevator moved by code is a kinematic body such as Godot's AnimatableBody2D.
statements.explanation: A kinematic body is moved by code or animation and still pushes others.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The player is a character body such as Godot's CharacterBody2D.
statements.explanation: A character body is code-driven with collision detection and no simulation.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A pushable crate is a static body.
statements.explanation: A pushable crate is a dynamic (rigid) body.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The level floor is a static body.
statements.explanation: A floor is a fixed obstacle.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A health pickup is a trigger region such as an Area2D that does not block.
statements.explanation: A pickup detects the player and does not block.

questions.stem: A developer asks for a crate knocked away by an explosion, a rocket that accelerates while its engine burns, and a character that moves at 200 px/s while a key is held. Check each statement that is true about choosing force, impulse or setting velocity.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The rocket's thrust is a force applied on each physics step while the engine burns.
statements.explanation: Sustained thrust is a force over time.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The explosion knock-back is a force applied on each physics step.
statements.explanation: A one-time knock-back is an impulse, not a continuing force.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The 200 px/s character on a character body is moved by setting its velocity.
statements.explanation: The code owns a character body's motion, so it sets velocity.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Impulse is divided by velocity to give the change in mass.
statements.explanation: The change in velocity is the impulse divided by mass.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Applying an impulse once per rendered frame makes the total push depend on the frame rate.
statements.explanation: Frames per second differ between machines, so the number of impulses per second differs.

questions.stem: A team talks about its documents before building a 2D platformer. The words pitch, brief, GDD and pillar get mixed up. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A design pillar is a planned feature in the backlog, such as double jump.
statements.explanation: A pillar is a short statement of the intended experience, not a feature.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A GDD is the source code of the mechanics written in prose, so editing the document edits the game.
statements.explanation: A GDD describes intended behaviour; code is the implementation.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A GDD is frozen at the start of production so playtest findings do not change it.
statements.explanation: A GDD is revised as prototypes and playtests teach the team; an unrevised one becomes stale.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A pitch or brief states the core idea and scope in short form, and the GDD develops those decisions in detail.
statements.explanation: The brief is the compact form; the GDD is the detailed one.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A game design document (GDD) records what the game is and how it should behave, in enough detail for builders and testers to work from.
statements.explanation: A GDD is the detailed shared description of intended behaviour.

questions.stem: A team has the design pillars "fast restarts", "readable danger" and "one-button depth". Late in development someone proposes a 30-second unskippable cutscene after each death. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: "Make the game fun" works well as a pillar because it excludes no feature.
statements.explanation: A pillar that excludes nothing settles no decision.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The cutscene conflicts with the pillar "fast restarts", so the pillar gives grounds to reject or change it.
statements.explanation: A pillar is used to test a proposal against the intended experience.

statements.label: C
statements.text: "Enemies flash 0.4 s before an attack lands" is a requirement, because a test can check it.
statements.explanation: A requirement states something checkable; a pillar guides judgement.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A feature list and a set of pillars are the same document under two names.
statements.explanation: A feature list names things to build; pillars name the experience.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A design pillar is a short statement of the experience the game aims to deliver, used to judge proposed features.
statements.explanation: Pillars are a decision tool.

questions.source: Core loop versus game loop, meta loop
questions.stem: In a roguelike the player enters a room, fights, picks up a reward and enters the next room. When a run ends, the player spends currency on permanent upgrades and starts a new run. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: The engine's game loop (read input, update, draw each frame) is the same thing as the core loop.
statements.explanation: The game loop is a programming construct; the core loop is a design term about what the player repeats.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The core loop is the short cycle of player actions repeated most often, here enter, fight and collect.
statements.explanation: The core loop is the moment-to-moment cycle the rest of the game is built around.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A loop in the design sense has an action, an outcome and feedback that leads into the next action.
statements.explanation: Feedback closes the cycle and motivates repeating it.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Spending currency between runs belongs to a meta loop (progression loop) wrapped around the core loop.
statements.explanation: Loops nest: a longer progression loop surrounds the short core loop.

statements.label: E
statements.text: The core loop is a list of features grouped by importance and by the team that builds each.
statements.explanation: A feature list is not a repeated cycle.

questions.stem: Two requirements arrive for one game. One says "The player can interact with the world." The other says "The player can jump, dash and grapple." A player verb is an action the player chooses to perform. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Jump, dash and grapple are player verbs.
statements.explanation: The player chooses when to perform each.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A verb is buildable once it has a name; the input, the effect and the feedback can be left to the agent.
statements.explanation: A buildable verb states its input, its rule for what changes, and the feedback the player perceives.

statements.label: C
statements.text: "Interact" is a vague verb, since it names no input, target or change of state.
statements.explanation: A coding agent cannot tell what to build from it.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A genre fixes the verbs, so choosing a verb list is a label and not a design decision.
statements.explanation: Choosing and limiting verbs is a central design choice.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Health regeneration is a player verb because it affects the outcome.
statements.explanation: The player does not choose it; it is a system rule.

questions.stem: The MDA framework separates mechanics (rules and systems the designer builds), dynamics (behaviour that emerges when players use the rules) and aesthetics (the emotional responses of players). A designer adds a rule to a shooter: the player carries at most 12 rounds. Players start hoarding rounds and avoiding fights, and report feeling tense. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A dynamic can be read off the rule text, so a playtest adds no information about it.
statements.explanation: Dynamics appear when players meet the rules, so they are found by observing play.

statements.label: B
statements.text: The 12-round limit is a mechanic.
statements.explanation: It is a rule the designer wrote.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Hoarding rounds and avoiding fights is a dynamic.
statements.explanation: It emerges from players meeting the rule and is not a line in the rules.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The designer sets an aesthetic directly by writing the feeling into the rules.
statements.explanation: Aesthetics are players' responses; the designer can only shape rules that tend to produce them.

statements.label: E
statements.text: Tension is an aesthetic.
statements.explanation: Aesthetics are the felt experience.

questions.stem: A designer wants a stealth meter that fills while an enemy can see the player. Sort what is built from what emerges using mechanic, dynamic and aesthetic. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Players waiting at cover for a patrol gap is an aesthetic.
statements.explanation: That is behaviour that emerges, so it is a dynamic.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Players rushing between blind spots is a mechanic because the player performs it.
statements.explanation: Emergent player behaviour is a dynamic; the mechanic is the rule that makes it worthwhile.

statements.label: C
statements.text: The rule "the meter fills at a set rate while seen and drains when unseen" is a mechanic.
statements.explanation: It is a rule the designer builds.

statements.label: D
statements.text: The satisfaction of slipping past a guard is a dynamic.
statements.explanation: A felt response is an aesthetic.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A fill rate per second and the threshold at which enemies attack are parameters of the mechanic, and a test can check them.
statements.explanation: Numbers and observable results make a mechanic buildable and checkable.

questions.stem: A team plans three builds: a weekend build of the core mechanic with placeholder boxes, a vertical slice, and a minimum viable product (MVP). Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: A minimum viable product (MVP) is the smallest complete game that can be released to real players.
statements.explanation: It has the minimum feature set but is complete and releasable.

statements.label: B
statements.text: A vertical slice is a thin portion of the game built to near-final quality across art, audio, UI and rules.
statements.explanation: Slice means deep, not wide.

statements.label: C
statements.text: A prototype is a quick build made to answer a design question, and may be thrown away.
statements.explanation: Prototypes are tools for learning, not products.

statements.label: D
statements.text: A prototype needs final art and audio, otherwise testers can not judge the mechanic.
statements.explanation: Placeholder art is normal for a prototype.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A vertical slice is a rough version of the whole game with the full set of levels present but unpolished.
statements.explanation: That describes a horizontal pass.

questions.stem: A studio pitches a 2D stealth puzzle game with thirty levels. Match each build to its term. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: Adding the long-term feature roadmap to an MVP keeps it minimum.
statements.explanation: Adding roadmap features grows the scope beyond minimum.

statements.label: B
statements.text: One finished level with final art, sound, UI and saving, built to show the whole game can reach that standard, is a vertical slice.
statements.explanation: A slice shows near-final quality across disciplines.

statements.label: C
statements.text: One room with a guard and a hiding spot built from placeholder boxes, to ask whether hiding is fun, is a prototype.
statements.explanation: It tests one design question.

statements.label: D
statements.text: Polishing a prototype's art before its design question is answered mixes up prototype and vertical slice, and delays learning.
statements.explanation: Confusing the builds spends effort on the wrong question.

statements.label: E
statements.text: A handful of levels with menus and saving, released to test whether players want the game, is a vertical slice.
statements.explanation: That is an MVP.

questions.stem: Four weeks before a deadline a team has one working level, and a teammate proposes online co-op, a crafting system and ten new enemy types. Check each statement that is true.

statements.label: A
statements.text: An out-of-scope list records non-goals already decided, so a proposal for one is declined without a new argument.
statements.explanation: A written non-goal turns a repeated argument into a settled decision.

statements.label: B
statements.text: Scope is the set of features and content a team commits to deliver by a date.
statements.explanation: Scope is a commitment tied to a date.

statements.label: C
statements.text: Small additions are not scope creep, because a small feature adds no schedule cost.
statements.explanation: Small additions add up, and each needs design, building and testing.

statements.label: D
